actions.cause: Location: Back Forty earns 43% less expected win per available hour than Center Pit at the same title (CI 41–44%), because fewer guests sit down there (occupancy 0.28 vs 0.42), not because of its games
actions.assumptions: Each machine's expected win per available hour = base × zone effect × title effect (R² 0.97). Swapping a strong title out of the Back Forty with a weak title in Center Pit/Main Entrance adds (zone gap) × (title gap). 28 effective days after 2-day lead; minus 3 h downtime per moved machine ($322). Low = 5th percentile of parameter draws AND only half the zone effect transfers; high = 95th percentile scaled up by how much the real M-1152 move beat the model. Check: the model predicts +82% for the one real B40→Main Entrance move (M-1152, Feb 4); observed +106% vs floor (95% CI 82–136%). Partners are all machines flagged 'Weak game for its spot' in section 6. Title effects estimated separately in the Back Forty and in prime zones correlate 0.97, so a title keeps its relative earning power when moved; tighter games draw only slightly less play (10% more house edge → 2% less coin-in/h), with no extra penalty in prime zones. Adding 8 machines to Center Pit in March raised zone coin-in ~18% without taking play from existing machines, so we assume no cannibalisation. We fund only the 3 swaps whose gain pays back their two moves inside July; 9 more Back Forty ↔ prime swaps (Prairie Thunder ↔ Comet Cash, +$974/day together) gain less than they cost in 28 days and are queued for August.
actions.measurement: Difference-in-differences over July: swapped machines' theo per available hour, before vs after, against unmoved machines of the same titles in the same zones; plus total zone coin-in for B40, PIT and ENT to catch cannibalisation. Success = combined theo/h of the 6 moved machines up ≥10% vs control; if met, run the queued swaps in August.
